newsitem.title: UK: Wm Cook sets buyout to trump Triplex.
newsitem.headline: Wm Cook sets buyout to trump Triplex.

text.p: Determined managers at British steel castings specialist William Cook Plc launched an 80 million pound ($130) ($131 million), venture capital-backed buyout bid for the company on Thursday in an attempt to thwart hostile bidder Triplex Lloyd Plc.
In a move that brought new big guns onto the field of a bloody two-month battle, Cook's executive chairman Andrew Cook rolled out investors Electra Fleming as his latest weapon.
The venture capital specialist is a joint venture of Electra Investment Trust Plc and privately-owned British investment bank Robert Fleming.

They said their bid would offer William Cook shareholders 425 pence cash per unit, compared with a full cash alternative of 383.4 pence per share in Triplex Lloyd's latest bid and a share-based alternative worth about 400 pence.
Electra Fleming director Tim Syder told Reuters the company had been in touch with William Cook for about three weeks and was "impressed by the team" at the automotive industry supplier.
After initial due diligence, "our conclusion is we find it an attractive investment opportunity", he told Reuters.

The institution would now present its terms to Cook's other shareholders, he added, and would explain that as well as backing the existing management Electra Fleming would also set them new goals under an incentive package.

A spokeswoman for diversified engineering company Triplex Lloyd Plc -- whose latest offer launched earlier this week valued William Cook at about 74 million pounds -- said it would be looking at its options after the buyout move.
One of these routes was to raise its bid, although it has already done this once.

She added that Triplex's initial reaction was that the management buyout (mbo) approach did nothing to address what it believes are deficiencies in William Cook's management and its record under Andrew Cook.

"The company (Triplex) will be looking at its options, but I think the institutional investors should realise that this (mbo) is just a company that's been set up as a defensive move by this individual (Andrew Cook), who doesn't want to lose the reins he's been holding on to," the spokeswoman said.
She added that shareholders should consider that by opting for a deal with Triplex Lloyd, William Cook would become part of a group "that is going to grow it forwards".
Triplex Lloyd's share-based bid is worth around 400 pence per share, but its cash alternative offers a lower 383.4 pence.

Share analysts have said they believe that significant William Cook shareholders are looking for an exit price of at least 400 pence, preferably in cash, in which case the current Triplex bid may be seen as falling short.
By the close of business at 1630 GMT, William Cook's share price had jumped 45 pence on the day to 420 pence, just under the mbo bid level. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
